correctness.rationale: Equation (2) of Zhao–Ma confirms the three updates and K=64 μ, with μ positive. At w=0 the last output vanishes; the middle equation gives (K-1)v=j=floor(Kv). Thus for 0<K<1 the origin is the only candidate; for K=1 all v are possible and no first-coordinate wrap is needed, giving the fixed curve. For K>1 the half-open inequality gives 0≤j<K-1, and Kv_j=j+v_j. Solving the first equation gives u=(Kv_j-m)/(1+Kv_j) with exactly the j+1 admissible integers 0≤m≤j. Summing yields the stated triangular count; at K=r the last candidate v=1 is absent and for K just above r its new row contains r points. This agrees with N(64)=2016 and N(K)=32640 for 255<K≤255.936. For j≥1 both first outputs are strictly interior, and all three arguments stay on the chosen branches on the positive-w side close to the state. The derivatives of the third equation through U,V vanish at w=0; triangularity gives -Kv_j,K,K(1+(u+v)/64), with Kv_j>1. At the origin the nonnegative domain gives the right derivatives and multipliers 0,K,K. For integer r, write h=1/(r-1) and bin 2v by [jh,(j+1)h). Then a_j-b_j=[r-2(j+1)]/[r(r-1)²], so moving target v mass to endpoints and adjusting row weights costs at most 3h/2. In a row with j+1 atoms the sorted horizontal points each lie in their corresponding equal-width quantile bin; replacing them by uniform u costs at most 1/[2(j+1)] per row, or 1/r on average. Combining gives 1/r+3h/2≤5h/2, also proving the frozen (looser) 6h bound. The distribution is empirical over fixed states on the face, not an invariant density for typical or full-cube trajectories.

The distinct claim is the full positive-real-gain face census, including strict half-open border jumps and a resonance curve, accompanied by the transverse branch spectrum and an explicit nonuniform spatial law. The primary model and close same-map inverse results give part of the arithmetic, but not this combined classification or limit. This is an evidence-limited assessment, not a claim of worldwide priority.

value.rationale: An exact count and location of equilibria on a built-in invariant face complement the published map's numerical bifurcation studies. The continuum-to-staircase resonance, row creation at an excluded edge, expanding one-sided spectrum, and a nonuniform limiting spatial law together describe a natural piece of this model's dynamics. The contribution is scoped: the asymptotic formally continues the same formula beyond the experimental range, and the boundary points do not diagnose interior or implementation behavior.
